_comment: 🛑🛑 TRANSLATOR: READ `crustify-bridge3/AGENT-BRIEF.md` IN FULL BEFORE YOU EDIT ANYTHING, then
`crustify-bridge3/TASK.md` and `crates/compiler/deeptools/CLAUDE.md`. All three outrank the
generic C-porting conventions in your system prompt, and the FIRST of them carries HARD CAPS that
a batch will be sent back for exceeding. Your prompt does not name them, which is why they are
named here — this file is the campaign-wide config your prompt DOES name.
Campaign-wide inventory for bridge 3: SentientIR -> ProgIR, dcc pass D76, the last MLIR rung.
130 functions from dcc/src/Conversion/SentientToProgIR/, 6,879 declaration lines, 8 dependency
levels. They land in the existing crate `deeptools` under src/bridges/sentient_to_progir/.
⛔ NONE OF THE C-WRAPPING CONVENTIONS APPLY. There is no C left anywhere: no bindgen, no -sys
crate, no `ffi::`, no `mod ffi_export`, no `#[unsafe(no_mangle)] extern "C"`, no
Foo/FooRef/FooMut triple, no `unsafe`, no CRUSTIFY_<FILE> switch, no C build, no sanitizers and
no io_equiv harness. The reference is a compiler that does not run on this host. This is a
pure-logic port of C++ into an existing Rust crate. The only anchor you emit is
`/// Replaces: eNNN_name`.
⛔ THE CRATE NEVER RUNTIME REFUSES: no Result, no Err(, no .ok_or, no assert!, no debug_assert!.
A closed set is an enum; an invariant is a type; a -1 sentinel is an Option. `todo!` naming an
unported op is tolerated. This span has FOUR checking functions (checkRegDefs,
verifyOnTheFlyConversions, and the validity/signalPassFailure paths in runOnOperation) — port each
as a function that RETURNS THE OFFENDERS, the way progir::Program::overflowing already does.
⛔ THE OP A FUNCTION EMITS IS THE FUNCTION. A previous attempt extracted each function's decision
rule into a documented predicate, left out the emission, and reported it done — nothing called any
of it. What you MAY drop is the mechanism for reaching operands (walking uses, memoising by
(core, corelet, component), positioning an OpBuilder), because the C++ builds an IR at run time
and this crate builds a typed value at compile time. What you may NOT drop is what is emitted, or
with which attribute names and values, or the branch order, or the early returns.
⛔ IF THE TARGET ISLAND CANNOT EXPRESS SOMETHING, EXTEND THE ISLAND (src/islands/progir/, 571
lines and deliberately small). Deciding a function is unnecessary is not the porter's call.
OpCode and OperandField are already vendored in sys-arch-spec (91 opcodes, 89 operand fields) —
never hand-transcribe a second copy of either.
⛔ YOUR GATE IS `cargo check -p deeptools` AND `cargo test -p deeptools`, ONCE PER BATCH at the
end. Do NOT run the workspace build or the acceptance build: this host is near capacity and two
sibling campaigns are running. The orchestrator owns that gate.
⛔ THERE IS NO CODEQL DATABASE AND NO WAVEFRONT EXTRACTION FOR THIS CAMPAIGN, and that is a
decision, not an omission:
1. The campaign's C++ surface is ONE self-contained translation unit,
crustify-bridge3/cpp/bridge3.cpp, whose 130 function bodies call names that exist only as a
NAME CATALOGUE in cpp/prelude.inc. A call graph over a catalogue has no edges to give.
2. The dependency order is already AUTHORITATIVE and machine-readable: bridge3.cpp is emitted
in dependency order with LEVEL banners (level 0 calls nothing else in the span, level N only
levels below), and every entry carries its original dcc/src/<file>:<line> citation.
crustify-bridge3/UNITS.tsv and crates/compiler/deeptools/docs/bridge3-porting-order.md list
all 130 in that order, with the Rust home for each.
3. The levels are computed over the SCC CONDENSATION of the call graph, because the span is
mutually recursive: LowerUniformOperations and GenerateProgIR call each other and share
level 5. A plain longest-path fixpoint ran away and printed 'level 266'.
The wave plans under crustify/campaigns/bridge3/ are authored from those level banners.
This file is the provenance the schedules record and hash. Keep it byte-stable while a wave is
in flight: `crustify translate` rejects a schedule whose oracle config changed since planning.
_comment_authority: THE ULTIMATE AUTHORITY IS THE C++ TREE, NOT THE EXTRACT:
which is exactly the revision every banner cites.
✅ THIS EXTRACT IS VERIFIED UNTRUNCATED: 130 of 130. crustify-bridge3/tools/verify_extract3.py
does not import the extractor's scanner — it re-derives every function's end from the authority
with its own character-state-machine brace matcher and compares LINE COUNTS, non-whitespace
CHARACTER counts and then full CONTENT, and separately asserts each body's last non-blank line
closes its function and equals the authority's own last line. TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS confirm it
bites: a tail cut re-balanced with a bare `}` and a brace-neutral 4-line cut from a body's middle
were both CAUGHT. Re-run it with `--self-test` to see both.
So you may read bridge3.cpp as complete. Still open the authority file at the cited line for a
long body: it has the surrounding declarations the extract does not.
⛔ BRIDGE 2's EXTRACT WAS NOT LIKE THIS. It truncated 366 of 384 bodies while its check reported
'verbatim, 12 sampled, none differed', because the check re-sliced the source with the SAME
(file, line, length) the extractor had used — it compared what was copied against what was
copied. If you are looking at crustify-bridge2/source/bridge2.cpp you are in the wrong campaign.
⛔ /Users/nickm/git/deeptools is a DIFFERENT revision. Do not use it.
_comment_not_this_campaign: ⛔⛔ dcc/src/Transform/Sentient/ — 32,766 lines of D29-D75 passes — IS A SEPARATE, LARGER BODY OF
WORK AND MUST NOT BE PULLED IN. Those passes rewrite SentientIR IN PLACE before D76 runs:
AddressPinningAndToggle.cpp, LiveRangeReduction.cpp, OpRerolling.cpp, LoopRolling.cpp and forty
more. They are island-internal transforms, not this conversion.
If a function you port depends on state those passes establish — register assignments, pinned
addresses, rerolled loops — port the conversion AS THE REFERENCE WRITES IT and record the
dependency in the commit message. Do NOT port the pass, and do NOT invent the state.
